title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 105
paragraphs: First of all, while they were still in the city, the generals dispatched a herald to Sparta — Pheidippides, an Athenian who was by profession a long-distance runner. As Pheidippides himself told the Athenians on his return, Pan met him on Mount Parthenion above Tegea; calling out his name, Pan told him to ask the Athenians why they gave him no attention, when he was well disposed toward them and had often been useful to them before, and would be useful again. The Athenians, when their fortunes had been set right, believed the tale to be true and established a temple to Pan below the Acropolis; and from that message on, they propitiate him with yearly sacrifices and a torch-race.
